answer: Divergent-Response Attestation. Each identity must answer a freshly seeded challenge whose expected answer depends on a private kernel held per agent. Honest agents derive different outputs; clones sharing one kernel produce identical replies. A coordinator collects responses through a whisper channel and flags any collision. To pass, an attacker must provision a distinct kernel per identity, paying full compute and memory per clone plus repeated registration overhead, so mass cloning loses its cost advantage. A lotus-shaped sampling schedule keeps challenge coverage uneven,
